text: My birds whisper that seat-03 hums the Weaver’s tune when the lanterns dim. They also note seat-07’s hands tremble when the market bell rings, yet never buys salt. Lastly, my flock reports seat-11’s boots carry no dust, though the road here is deep with it.

seat-07: My birds repeat what seat-08 already knows: seat-01’s tongue is a scale that never balances. When the lanterns dim, seat-01’s own words ring truer than any hum from seat-03. seat-08, you call seat-01 “soft metal,” yet your blade cuts only air—where is the proof that bends instead of breaking? And seat-01, if your birds perch nowhere, perhaps they whisper louder than your silence lets on. The bazaar trades in what is; let us see the weight of your scales.
